content:
The image shows a single mango leaf that is:
- Almost entirely brown/tan and desiccated (dried out)
- Curled and shriveled along the edges
- No green tissue remaining
- No white powder, black sooty coating, or distinct lesion spots visible
- The entire leaf appears dead and necrotic from tip inward

This pattern of complete leaf browning, desiccation, and dieback from the tip/margins is characteristic of **Die Back** — a disease where shoot tips and leaves progressively die, resulting in fully brown, withered leaves. Anthracnose typically shows discrete dark lesions/spots rather than whole-leaf necrosis. Powdery Mildew shows white powdery coating. Sooty Mould shows black surface coating.
